correctness.rationale: The frozen proof used a real logarithm of the expected signed output while allowing negative x0. The complete repaired result specifies real x0, takes logs of positive amplification factors for h small, and retains the Gaussian statement for either sign. Factoring the denominator shows no pole in the open left half-plane; its squared-modulus advantage over the numerator is −4 Re(z)(1+u(1−u)|z|²)>0. Compactness in u yields a uniform contraction for each fixed z, and a uniformly bounded intervening factor yields odd-iterate decay without monotonicity. For the original independent method and z=−x with x>2, the phase interval 0≤u≤1/x gives E|R|²≥(x/2−1)²/x, which diverges. For real λh, independent expansion of the pair log gives 2λh+(2/3−2C)λ³h³+O(h⁵) with C=U(1−U), and the single-step log gives λh+(U−1/2)λ²h²+O(h³). The uniform moments Var(C)=1/180 and Var(U)=1/12 follow by integrating the polynomials. The centered independent remainder sums are O(√M h⁵) and O(√M h³) in L², negligible at their respective scales, with M=T/(2h) and T/h. The ordinary iid CLT yields the log variances Tλ⁶/90 and Tλ⁴/12. Jensen centering differs by M log E exp(W_h), for centered log increments W_h=O(h³) and O(h²); expanding the exponential makes those differences O(h⁵) and O(h³). The output exponential delta method multiplies by x0² exp(2λT). This avoids taking a log of the signed output or assuming away deterministic bias.
residual_risks: The Gaussian limits apply to real scalar decay and iid uniform draws per independent unit of the method, not arbitrary laws or nonlinear vector equations. Pairwise A-stability is not per-step monotonicity, stiff L-stability or a deterministic error-order improvement.
